_note: <CodeBlock> — the monospaced source listing (U11). THE HIGHLIGHTER IS A SMALL LINE-LOCAL TOKENIZER carried in the component, never a highlighting library: chunk the line, then fold the chunks through a state machine where block comments carry across lines, line comments and quoted strings run to their end, and identifiers match the language's keyword set. Adjacent same-kind chunks MERGE, so a line costs a handful of text nodes rather than one per character - that merge is the difference between a listing and a render stall, so the token runs are pinned exactly, not just their kinds. An UNLISTED LANGUAGE GETS AN EMPTY KEYWORD SET and degrades to strings + numbers + comments; it never produces a wrong highlight. Colour is never the only signal: the source text is the content, an emphasised line also carries a gutter marker, and the whole listing reads to assistive tech as ONE utterance with the copy button labelled separately. The fold is written without loops because a computed value has no loop grammar - the first spelling used two nested `while`s over a pushed accumulator and rendered an EMPTY BLOCK on all three renderers.

cases.name: js: a keyword, a string, a number and a line comment, with same-kind runs merged
a block comment CARRIES ACROSS LINES and ends mid-line
an UNLISTED language keeps numbers but claims no keywords and no comments it cannot know
no language at all behaves exactly like an unlisted one
shell comments start at # and js comments do not
EMPTY: no source is still one row, so the block has a height
a blank line between two statements keeps its row and its number
an escaped quote does not close the string
an unterminated string runs to the end of its line and no further
the emphasised lines are a set of ONE-BASED numbers, trimmed
no highlight attribute marks nothing rather than marking line zero
the listing is ONE utterance: the language, then the source verbatim
with no language the utterance still names itself as code
the three display switches default off and are the string plane's true/1
wrap, gutter and copy switch on with "true"
the token tints are the four kinds plus a plain fallback
a comment is the quietest tint, a string the loudest
plain source text takes the label colour, never a highlight colour
